proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathscr E=\sigma(E_0)\).  Because \(z_0=\mathbb E[Z_j\mid E_0]\) is \(\mathscr E\)-measurable, conditioning on \((z_0,E_0)\) is the same as conditioning on \(E_0\) for the variables below.  By \texttt{def:target} and linearity of conditional expectation,
\[
\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{
\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0,E_0]
-\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]
\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:consistency} and the definition of \(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\) give
\[
\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0,E_0]
=\mathbb E_P[\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0].
\tag{2}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-transport} gives
\[
\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]
=m_s(z_{0s}).
\tag{3}
\]
Substitution of (2)--(3) into (1) proves the identifying equality.  Assumption \texttt{ass:historical-regression} separately makes \(m_s\) the observed-law conditional mean learned from the untreated pseudo-event blocks.  Thus event transport and consistency prove the relationship between the causal target and the observed-law functional; the relationship is not part of the target's definition.

Fix a successful cohort \(s\), abbreviate \(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}\) by \(\bar B_s\), and fix \(\gamma\in\mathbb R^{q_r}\).  The event part of the criterion in \texttt{def:fwl-regression} satisfies the exact sum-of-squares identity
\[
\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\theta-e_0^\top\gamma)^2
=\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\bar B_s)^2
+(\bar B_s-\theta-e_0^\top\gamma)^2.
\tag{4}
\]
For fixed \(\gamma\), the unique minimizing event coefficient is therefore
\[
\widehat\theta_s=\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^\top\gamma.
\tag{5}
\]
At (5), the event criterion is independent of \(\gamma\), so the profiled criterion, apart from the first constant in (4), is
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
w_{st}\{Q_{sti}-b_r(u_{st})^\top\gamma\}^2.
\tag{6}
\]
This is precisely the historical weighted least-squares problem in \texttt{def:feasible-estimator}.  Passage of the normalized Gram-shape test implies \(G_s\succeq c_GL_sI\succ0\), so (6) has the unique minimizer \(\widehat\gamma_s\).  Hence
\[
\widehat\theta_s=\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_s.
\tag{7}
\]
Finally, the definitions of \(\widehat m_s\), \(\theta_{\mathrm{FWL}}\), and \(\widehat\tau\) yield
\[
\theta_{\mathrm{FWL}}
=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_s)
=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s(\bar B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat m_s)
=\widehat\tau.
\]
This last identity is algebraic on every sample on which all selected fits exist.

Fix a regular conditional law given \(E_0\), and write
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:1\le s\le S,\ 1\le t\le T\}.
\]
Choose all numerical constants in the nonempty interior of the fixed support, Holder, covariance, and modulus envelopes, and place the query in a fixed compact subset of \(\mathcal Z_+\) inside \(([0,1]^d)^S\).  In every experiment below, draw bounded event outcomes independently of \(\mathscr X\).  Conditional on \(\mathscr X\), draw bounded historical response paths independently across units from possibly heterogeneous kernels sharing the conditional mean \(m_s(X_{st})\).  It follows directly that
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\tag{40}
\]
Complete the unobserved event-date untreated potential outcomes so that their cohort-average conditional means are \(m_s(z_{0s})\).  Set observed and historical potential outcomes according to consistency, make historical potential outcomes invariant to the event treatment, and make every potential outcome invariant to other units' assignments.  This verifies consistency, historical consistency, limited anticipation, no spillovers, and event transport.  Draw donors conditionally iid, independently of the panel, with covariance and standardized fourth moment strictly inside the declared envelopes, and set \(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\).  Bounded response kernels, design laws, carriers, and donors are chosen as specified channel by channel below.  Thus (40) verifies exactly the two additional full-design restrictions, while identical within-site laws and a response-variance lower bound are not class requirements.

If \(p,p+v\in[\eta,1-\eta]\), Taylor's theorem applied to binary relative entropy gives
\[
\operatorname{kl}(p+v,p)\le\frac{v^2}{2\eta(1-\eta)}.
\tag{41}
\]
Conditional product structure makes the divergence of each response experiment the sum of these conditional binary divergences.

For the treated channel put \(V_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\) and change the event response probability in cohort \(s\) by
\[
v_s=c_0\frac{\pi_s}{n_sV_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}}.
\]
Since \(V_{\mathrm{tr}}\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\), \(|v_s|\le c_0n_s^{-1/2}\); sufficiently small fixed \(c_0\) keeps all probabilities in \([\eta,1-\eta]\).  The target separation and divergence satisfy
\[
\sum_s\pi_sv_s=c_0V_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2}=c_0R_{\mathrm{tr}}^{1/2},
\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{tr}},P_{0,\mathrm{tr}})
\le C\sum_sn_sv_s^2=Cc_0^2.
\tag{42}
\]

For the smoothing channel choose \(s_*\) maximizing \(\pi_s^2(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\), set \(b=(Tn_{s_*})^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\), and perturb only that cohort by
\[
m_{s_*,1}(x)-m_{s_*,0}(x)
=c_1b^\lambda\psi((x-z_{0s_*})/b),
\tag{43}
\]
where \(\psi\) is a fixed compactly supported \(\lambda\)-Holder bump with \(\psi(0)=1\).  Use a common affine carrier with nonzero covariance-standardized gradient when \(\lambda>1\), and a common asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp carrier when \(0<\lambda\le1\).  The increment calculation in the proof of \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-spacing-obstruction}, with \(b\) in place of \(h_T\), shows that sufficiently small fixed \(c_1\) preserves the response interior, Holder radius, and both sides of the local-modulus inequality.  Because \(S\) is fixed,
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sm}}}(z_0)|^2
=c_1^2\pi_{s_*}^2b^{2\lambda}\ge cR_{\mathrm{sm}}.
\tag{44}
\]
The design probability of the bump support is at most \(Cb^d\), so (41), integrated over the design and summed over the \(Tn_{s_*}\) observations, gives
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{sm}},P_{0,\mathrm{sm}})
\le CTn_{s_*}b^{2\lambda+d}=C.
\tag{45}
\]
An iid uniform design verifies the design-only mixing condition in this channel.

For the spacing channel take the pair constructed in \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-spacing-obstruction}.  It satisfies (40), the marginal density bounds, design-only geometric mixing, and the two-sided modulus.  Its observed laws coincide on a no-active-block event of probability bounded away from zero, and
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,\mathrm{sp}}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,\mathrm{sp}}}(z_0)|^2
\ge c\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{2\lambda/d}
=cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{46}
\]
Hence this pair has positive testing affinity; no Kullback--Leibler bound is asserted.

For the donor channel retain the same affine or asymmetric-cusp carrier.  By the lower local-modulus inequality, for \(\delta=c_2N^{-1/2}\le\delta_0\), the supremum in \texttt{def:local-modulus} supplies an admissible \(u_N\), chosen to attain at least half the supremum, such that
\[
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2\le c_2N^{-1/2},
\qquad
\left|\sum_s\pi_s\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{N,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\ge cN^{-\kappa/2}.
\tag{47}
\]
Choose a fixed common-support finite distribution on \(\mathbb R^{Sd}\) whose support affinely spans \(\mathbb R^{Sd}\), whose covariance lies strictly inside the ellipticity envelope, and whose atom probabilities lie strictly inside the probability simplex.  Perturb those probabilities along a bounded score whose mean shift is \(u_N\).  The spanning property solves the finite linear mean equations, and interiority keeps all probabilities positive for sufficiently small \(c_2\).  Continuity preserves the covariance and fourth-moment envelopes.  Taylor expansion of the finite probability-vector likelihood, whose Hessian is bounded on this compact simplex neighborhood, yields
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_{1,\mathrm{don}},P_{0,\mathrm{don}})
\le CN\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_N\|_2^2\le Cc_2^2.
\tag{48}
\]
Keep the observed event mean fixed and complete untreated event potential outcomes under each law with cohort means equal to the corresponding surface at the corresponding donor mean.  The identifying equality in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} turns (47) into a target separation whose square is at least \(cR_{\mathrm{don}}\).

For any two laws, apply data processing to \(A=\{dP_1/dP_0\ge1\}\).  Twice differentiating binary relative entropy shows that it is at least twice the squared difference of the two event probabilities.  Hence
\[
\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)\ge2\|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}^2,
\qquad
\int\min\{dP_0,dP_1\}
\ge1-\sqrt{\operatorname{KL}(P_1,P_0)/2}.
\tag{49}
\]
Reducing \(c_0,c_1,c_2\) makes (49) uniformly positive for the treated, smoothing, and donor pairs; (46) supplies affinity directly for spacing.  The causal completions preceding (41) verify membership in the same enlarged full-design-centered class for all four pairs, proving every assertion.

For channel \(q\), take \((P_{0,q},P_{1,q})\) from \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}, write its target values as \(\theta_0,\theta_1\), and put \(\Delta_q=|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  The pair has affinity at least \(a_0>0\) and \(\Delta_q^2\ge cR_q\).  For any estimator \(\widetilde\tau\), the events
\[
E'_0=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_0|\ge\Delta_q/2\},
\qquad
E'_1=\{|\widetilde\tau-\theta_1|\ge\Delta_q/2\}
\]
cover the sample space.  Integrating against the overlap measure gives
\[
P_{0,q}(E'_0)+P_{1,q}(E'_1)\ge a_0,
\]
and hence
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}
[(\widetilde\tau-\theta_\ell)^2\mid E_0]
\ge\frac{a_0\Delta_q^2}{8}\ge cR_q.
\tag{50}
\]
Maximizing over the four channels and using \(R_{\star,\beta}=\max_qR_q\), then taking the supremum over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\) and the infimum over estimators, proves the lower bound.

For the upper bound put \(\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:s\le S,t\le T\}\), and condition on \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\).  On the event of successful fits, \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and the linear representation in \texttt{def:honest-interval} give
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=U_{\mathrm{evt}}-U_{\mathrm{hist}}-B_{\mathrm{LP}}-B_{\mathrm{don}},
\tag{51}
\]
where
\[
U_{\mathrm{evt}}=\sum_{s,i}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\},
\qquad
U_{\mathrm{hist}}=\sum_{s,i}\pi_s\sum_t a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti},
\]
\[
B_{\mathrm{LP}}=\sum_s\pi_s
\left\{\sum_{t,i}a_{sti}m_s(X_{st})-m_s(\widetilde z_s)\right\},
\qquad
B_{\mathrm{don}}=\sum_s\pi_s
\{m_s(\widetilde z_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}.
\]
The two full-design restrictions center the first two sums under the displayed conditioning.  Conditional cross-unit independence and the range bound \(B\) yield
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{evt}}^2\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
\le B^2\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}=B^2R_{\mathrm{tr}},
\tag{52}
\]
and \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} yields
\[
\mathbb E_P[U_{\mathrm{hist}}^2\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]
\le B^2\sum_{s,i}\left[\pi_s\sum_t|a_{sti}|\right]^2
\le B^2c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\tag{53}
\]
The entire calendar response path of one unit is one cluster in (53); no temporal outcome restriction or identical unit law is used.

If \(C_K\) bounds the Euclidean radius of the kernel support, then \(\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_s\|_2\le C_Kh_s\) whenever \(w_{st}>0\).  The deterministic weight bound and the Holder Taylor remainder give
\[
|B_{\mathrm{LP}}|\le C\sum_s\pi_sh_s^\lambda.
\tag{54}
\]
By Cauchy--Schwarz, \((\sum_s\pi_sh_s^\lambda)^2\le S\sum_s\pi_s^2h_s^{2\lambda}\).  Apply \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} with exponent \(2\lambda\).  Since \(S\) and the positive weights are fixed,
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{LP}}^2\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}+N^{-\lambda}\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta},
\tag{55}
\]
where \(N^{-\lambda}\le N^{-\kappa}\) because \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).

Put
\[
W_N=N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{N}Y_j,
\qquad Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0).
\]
Donor replication gives independent mean-zero vectors satisfying \(\mathbb E[Y_jY_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D\).  Expanding \(\|W_N\|_2^4\), all terms with a singleton index vanish.  The all-equal terms and the three pairings give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[\|W_N\|_2^4\mid E_0]
&=\frac1N\mathbb E_P[\|Y_1\|_2^4\mid E_0]\\
&\quad+\left(1-\frac1N\right)
\{(\operatorname{tr}I_D)^2+2\operatorname{tr}(I_D^2)\}\\
&\le \frac BN+\left(1-\frac1N\right)(D^2+2D)=M_4(N).
\end{aligned}
\tag{56}
\]
Consequently
\[
\mathbb E_P\left[
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\bar Z-z_0)\|_2^4\mid E_0\right]
\le CN^{-2}.
\tag{57}
\]
Euclidean projection onto the cube cannot increase distance from \(z_0\), and the eigenvalue bounds imply
\[
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z-z_0)\|_2
\le\sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\bar Z-z_0)\|_2.
\tag{58}
\]
On the event where the left side of (58) is at most \(\delta_0\), the upper local-modulus inequality bounds \(|B_{\mathrm{don}}|^2\) by its \(2\kappa\)-th power times a fixed constant.  Lyapunov's inequality and (57) bound the expectation by \(CN^{-\kappa}\).  On the complementary event, boundedness gives \(|B_{\mathrm{don}}|\le B\), while Markov's inequality and (57) give probability \(O(N^{-2})\).  Since \(0<\kappa\le1\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[B_{\mathrm{don}}^2\mid E_0]
\le CN^{-\kappa}=CR_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{59}
\]

Every successful intercept has absolute value at most \(B\sum_{t,i}|a_{sti}|\le Bc_G^{-1/2}\), and failed intercepts are zero.  Hence squared error is uniformly bounded on the bad sample.  The bad-sample bound in the selector lemma makes its contribution at most \(CR_{\star,\beta}\).  Combining (51)--(59) with \((x_1+\cdots+x_4)^2\le4\sum_jx_j^2\) proves
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\le CR_{\star,\beta}.
\tag{60}
\]
The same quantity upper-bounds the minimax infimum because \(\widehat\tau\) is a single observed-data estimator.

For completeness, let \(a=2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)\).  For every \(T\ge3\), weighted arithmetic--geometric mean and \(\log T\ge1\) give
\[
(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
=(n_s^{-1})^a(T^{-2\lambda/d})^{1-a}
\le an_s^{-1}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\]
After multiplying by \(\pi_s^2\), summing, and using \(\sum_s\pi_s^2\le1\),
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\le aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}
\le R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{61}
\]
Thus \(R_{\star,\beta}=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\) exactly for \(T\ge3\).  Equations (50) and (60) establish the asserted same-class bracket in every relative-growth regime.  The full donor covariance enters through the standardized modulus and (58), but neither the estimator nor the proof estimates it.

Let \(\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:s\le S,t\le T\}\), and condition on \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\).  On each successful fit, polynomial reproduction (12) applied to the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial of \(m_s\) at \(\widetilde z_s\), followed by (13), gives
\[
\left|e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_s-m_s(\widetilde z_s)
-\sum_{t,i}a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}\right|
\le C_{r,d}L\sum_{t,i}|a_{sti}|
\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_s\|_2^\lambda.
\tag{62}
\]
After cohort weighting, the right side is exactly \(A_L\).

Define the historical unit-cluster variables
\[
U_{si}=\pi_s\sum_t a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering} gives \(\mathbb E[U_{si}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]=0\): donor independence permits the donors to be added to the conditioning field.  Assumption \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} makes the variables independent over \((s,i)\) under that conditioning.  Since \(0\le Q_{sti}\le B\), the conditional range length of \(U_{si}\) is at most
\[
c_{si}=B\pi_s\sum_t|a_{sti}|.
\]
If a conditionally centered random variable \(U\) lies in an interval of length \(c\), convexity of \(x\mapsto e^{vx}\) bounds its conditional exponential moment by the endpoint mixture having the same mean.  Twice differentiating the logarithm of this mixture gives
\[
\mathbb E[e^{vU}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]\le e^{v^2c^2/8}.
\tag{63}
\]
Multiplication of (63) over the independent unit clusters, Chernoff's inequality, optimization over \(v>0\), and repetition for \(-U\) yield
\[
P\left\{
\left|\sum_{s,i}U_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}.
\tag{64}
\]
This uses no mixing or independence along the calendar within a unit.

Similarly define
\[
V_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability} centers \(V_{si}\) given \((\mathscr X,E_0)\), donor independence preserves that centering after adding the donors, and cross-unit independence makes the variables conditionally independent.  Their range lengths are at most \(B\pi_s/n_s\).  The same argument gives
\[
P\left\{
\left|\sum_{s,i}V_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{evt}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}.
\tag{65}
\]
The two events in (64)--(65) are combined by a union bound, so no independence between a unit's historical path and event outcome is needed.

For donor calibration put \(Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\) and \(W_N=N^{-1/2}\sum_jY_j\).  Conditional iid donor replication gives \(\mathbb E[Y_j\mid E_0]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[Y_jY_j^\top\mid E_0]=I_D\).  Expanding the fourth power and grouping the all-equal and three paired index patterns gives exactly
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[\|W_N\|_2^4\mid E_0]
&=\frac1N\mathbb E_P[\|Y_1\|_2^4\mid E_0]\\
&\quad+\left(1-\frac1N\right)
\{(\operatorname{tr}I_D)^2+2\operatorname{tr}(I_D^2)\}\\
&\le\frac BN+\left(1-\frac1N\right)(D^2+2D)
=M_4(N).
\end{aligned}
\tag{66}
\]
Define the donor-deviation event
\[
\mathcal D_N=\{\|W_N\|_2\le q_N\}.
\]
Markov's inequality and the definition of \(q_N\) imply
\[
P(\mathcal D_N^c\mid E_0)
\le\frac{M_4(N)}{q_N^4}=\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{67}
\]
Coordinatewise projection onto \([0,1]^{Sd}\) cannot increase Euclidean distance from \(z_0\), which lies in that cube.  The covariance eigenvalue bounds consequently give, on \(\mathcal D_N\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z-z_0)\|_2
&\le c_\Sigma^{-1/2}\|\widetilde z-z_0\|_2\\
&\le c_\Sigma^{-1/2}\|\bar Z-z_0\|_2\\
&\le\sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,q_N/\sqrt N
=\delta_N.
\end{aligned}
\tag{68}
\]
On the observable good event, \(\delta_N\le\delta_0\), so the upper half of \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus} and (68) imply
\[
\left|\sum_s\pi_s
\{m_s(\widetilde z_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta_N^\kappa=A_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{69}
\]

Let \(\mathcal G\) denote the selector-and-radius good event in \texttt{def:honest-interval}; it is measurable with respect to \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j))\).  On \(\mathcal G^c\), \(C_\alpha=[-B,B]\).  Each potential-outcome contrast lies in \([-B,B]\), and the cohort weights are positive and sum to one, so \(\tau_n(z_0)\in[-B,B]\) deterministically.  On \(\mathcal G\cap\mathcal D_N\), the identification equality, (62), and (69) decompose the estimator error into the event fluctuation, the historical fluctuation, and two terms bounded by \(A_L\) and \(A_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Hence noncoverage implies failure of (64) or (65).  Iterated conditioning gives the finite-sample bound
\[
\begin{aligned}
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\notin C_\alpha\mid E_0\}
&\le P(\mathcal D_N^c\mid E_0)\\
&\quad+\mathbb E\!\left[
\mathbf1_{\mathcal G\cap\mathcal D_N}
P\{\text{historical failure or event failure}
\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\}
\,\middle|\,E_0\right]\\
&\le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}
+\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}=\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\tag{70}
\]
No selector tail bound is used for (70).  Thus coverage is exact for every positive sample size and every law in the enlarged subclass.

For expected length, \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} gives deterministically on a successful fit
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\le B\left\{\tfrac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}})c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\}^{1/2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
=B\left\{\tfrac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}})R_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\}^{1/2}.
\tag{71}
\]
The kernel support and the same deterministic weight bound give
\[
A_L\le C\sum_s\pi_sh_s^\lambda.
\]
Applying the selector moment with exponent \(\lambda\), and using Cauchy--Schwarz across the fixed cohorts, gives
\[
\sup_P\mathbb E_P[A_L\mathbf1_{\mathcal G}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}^{1/2}
+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}+N^{-\lambda/2}\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{72}
\]
Since \(D\) and \(\alpha\) are fixed, (66) makes \(q_N\le C\), whence
\[
A_{\mathrm{don}}\le CN^{-\kappa/2}=CR_{\mathrm{don}}^{1/2}.
\tag{73}
\]
The selector lemma gives \(P(\mathcal G^c\mid E_0)\le CR_{\star,\beta}\) along the stated arrays.  The fallback length is at most \(2B\), and eventually \(R_{\star,\beta}\le R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\).  Since \(\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\le2H_\alpha\) on \(\mathcal G\), (71)--(73) prove
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]
\le C_\alpha^{\mathrm{up}}R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{74}
\]

For the lower bound, reduce the fixed perturbation constants in \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} so every channel affinity \(A_q\) exceeds \(2\alpha+a_0\) for a fixed \(a_0>0\); for the rare-block pair reduce its fixed active-block intensity.  Let \(I\) be finite-sample conditionally honest, let \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) be a channel pair's target values, and let \(\mu_q=P_{0,q}\wedge P_{1,q}\).  Uniform honesty and domination by the two laws imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_q\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I\}
&\ge\mu_q(\Omega)
-P_{0,q}\{\theta_0\notin I\}
-P_{1,q}\{\theta_1\notin I\}\\
&\ge A_q-2\alpha\ge a_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{75}
\]
On this event, \(\operatorname{length}(I)\ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  Therefore
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}[\operatorname{length}(I)\mid E_0]
\ge a_0|\theta_1-\theta_0|
\ge c_\alpha R_q^{1/2}.
\tag{76}
\]
Maximizing (76) over the four channels gives \(c_\alpha R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\).  If a sequence is only uniformly asymptotically conditionally honest, then for every \(\epsilon>0\) its two noncoverage probabilities are eventually at most \(\alpha+\epsilon\).  Choosing \(\epsilon<a_0/4\) replaces the final lower bound in (75) by \(a_0-2\epsilon\ge a_0/2\), proving the same rate.  Combining (70), (74), and (76) proves all claims.

Under the first specialization, \(S=1\) and \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\) imply \(\pi_1=1\).  The identification equality in \texttt{lem:identification-fwl} and \(m_1(x)=x+\Delta_0\) give
\[
\tau_n(z_0)
=\mathbb E_P[\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-m_1(z_{01})
=\mathbb E_P[\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,E_0]-z_{01}-\Delta_0.
\tag{77}
\]
When the proxy is the event cohort's baseline outcome, \(z_{01}\) is its conditional baseline mean.  When \(\Delta_0\) is the untreated cohort-average post-minus-baseline mean change, (77) is treated post minus treated baseline minus the untreated post-minus-baseline change.  This is the canonical conditional finite-cohort two-period difference-in-differences contrast.

For the second specialization define
\[
\tau_s=\frac1{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
\mathbb E_P[B_{si}(1)-B_{si}(0)\mid z_0,E_0].
\]
Homogeneity across cohorts states that \(\tau_s=\tau^{\mathrm{com}}\) for every \(s\).  By \texttt{def:target} and \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\),
\[
\tau_n(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\tau_s
=\tau^{\mathrm{com}}\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
=\tau^{\mathrm{com}}.
\tag{78}
\]
The stipulated absence of carry-over beyond \(h=0\) makes this common terminal-level contrast the contemporaneous finite-cohort effect on the buy-and-hold wealth level in \texttt{def:buyhold-level}.  That causal interpretation uses the stated specialization; it is not inferred from the algebra alone.

Suppress the cohort index, write \(\mathsf L=L_s\) and \(G=G_s\), and set \(v_{ti}=w_{st}^{1/2}b_r(u_{st})\).  Then
\[
G=\sum_{t,i}v_{ti}v_{ti}^\top,
\qquad
a_{sti}=w_{st}^{1/2}e_0^\top G^{-1}v_{ti}.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{t,i}|a_{sti}|
&\le
\left\{\sum_{t,i}(e_0^\top G^{-1}v_{ti})^2\right\}^{1/2}
\left\{\sum_{t,i}w_{st}\right\}^{1/2}\\
&=\{e_0^\top G^{-1}GG^{-1}e_0\}^{1/2}\mathsf L^{1/2}
=\{\mathsf Le_0^\top G^{-1}e_0\}^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
The selector requires \(G/\mathsf L\succeq c_GI\), whence \(G^{-1}\preceq(c_G\mathsf L)^{-1}I\).  Under the declared monomial normalization, \(e_0=b_r(0)\) is the constant-monomial coordinate and \(\|e_0\|_2=1\).  Therefore
\[
\mathsf Le_0^\top G^{-1}e_0\le c_G^{-1}.
\tag{9}
\]
For fixed \((s,t)\), neither \(u_{st}\) nor \(w_{st}\) depends on \(i\), while
\[
G_s=n_s\sum_tw_{st}b_r(u_{st})b_r(u_{st})^\top.
\]
Thus \(a_{sti}\) is constant in \(i\).  Equations (8)--(9) consequently imply
\[
\sum_t|a_{sti}|\le\frac{c_G^{-1/2}}{n_s}.
\tag{10}
\]
It follows that
\[
\sum_{s,i}\left[\pi_s\sum_t|a_{sti}|\right]^2
\le\sum_sn_s\left(\frac{\pi_sc_G^{-1/2}}{n_s}\right)^2
=c_G^{-1}\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
=c_G^{-1}R_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\tag{11}
\]
Finally, the normal equations reproduce every polynomial of total degree at most \(r\): for such a polynomial \(p\),
\[
\sum_{t,i}a_{sti}p(u_{st})=p(0).
\tag{12}
\]
Subtract the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial of \(m_s\) at \(\widetilde z_s\).  The Holder convention in \texttt{ass:holder-smoothness} gives
\[
|m_s(x)-T_{r,\widetilde z_s}m_s(x)|
\le C_{r,d}L\|x-\widetilde z_s\|_2^\lambda.
\tag{13}
\]
Multiplying (13) by \(|a_{sti}|\), summing, and applying the cohort weights gives exactly \(A_L\).  Neither (8) nor this Taylor calculation uses an upper bound on \(L_s\).

Condition throughout on \((E_0,\widetilde z_s=z)\).  By \texttt{ass:donor-independence}, this extra conditioning does not change the conditional law of the historical design.  By the revised \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}, that design process alone obeys the declared geometric absolute-regularity bound; no condition on the outcome path is used below.  For \(z\in[0,1]^d\) and \(0<h\le1\), define
\[
\ell_{z,h}(x)=K((x-z)/h),
\qquad
\Phi_{z,h}(x)=K((x-z)/h)b_r((x-z)/h)b_r((x-z)/h)^\top.
\]
Bounded support of \(K\), the density bounds, and the change of variables \(x=z+hu\) give a constant \(C_0<\infty\) such that
\[
\mathbb E_P[\ell_{z,h}(X_{st})\mid E_0]\le C_0h^d.
\tag{14}
\]
There is also a uniform lower bound.  Choose \(\eta>0\) and \(k_0>0\) such that \(K(u)\ge k_0\) on \([ -\eta,\eta]^d\).  For every \(z\) the rescaled cube contains one of the finitely many orthant boxes of side \(\eta\wedge(1/2)\).  On such a box a nonzero polynomial \(v^\top b_r(u)\) cannot vanish almost everywhere.  Compactness of the unit sphere in the fixed-dimensional space \(\mathbb R^{q_r}\), followed by the density lower bound, therefore yields \(c_0>0\) such that
\[
c_0h^d\le\mathbb E_P[\ell_{z,h}(X_{st})\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E_P[v^\top\Phi_{z,h}(X_{st})v\mid E_0]
\ge c_0h^d\|v\|_2^2.
\tag{15}
\]
These bounds are uniform in \(s,t,z,h\).  Fix \(0<c_G<c_0/(4C_0)\).

Let \(A_0>2\lambda/d+2\) and set
\[
b_T=\lceil C_\beta\log(T\vee2)\rceil,
\]
where \(C_\beta\) is sufficiently large that
\[
T\beta_0\rho_0^{b_T}\le T^{-A_0}.
\tag{16}
\]
Partition \(\{1,\ldots,T\}\) into consecutive blocks of length at most \(b_T\), and divide them into odd and even subfamilies.  Consecutive blocks of a fixed parity are separated by at least \(b_T\) calendar indices.  From the definition of the conditional absolute-regularity coefficient, replacing one such block by an independent copy with the same marginal changes the probability of every event by at most \(\beta_P(b_T\mid E_0)\).  Replacing the blocks successively and telescoping total-variation distances therefore shows that either parity subfamily differs from the product of its block marginals by at most
\[
C(T/b_T)\beta_P(b_T\mid E_0)\le CT^{-A_0}.
\tag{17}
\]

Let \(F\) be either \(\ell_{z,h}\) or \(v^\top\Phi_{z,h}v\) with \(\|v\|_2=1\), and let \(W_g\) be the sum of \(F(X_{st})\) over block \(g\) in one parity.  Boundedness of \(K\) and of \(b_r\) on the support of \(K\) implies
\[
0\le W_g\le Cb_T,
\qquad W_g^2\le Cb_TW_g.
\]
Under the product law in (17), the \(W_g\)'s are independent, and (14)--(15) imply
\[
\sum_g\operatorname{Var}(W_g)
\le\sum_g\mathbb E[W_g^2]
\le Cb_TTh^d.
\tag{18}
\]
For \(V_g=W_g-\mathbb EW_g\), expansion of the exponential series and the bounds \(|V_g|\le Cb_T\) and \(\mathbb E[V_g^2]=\operatorname{Var}(W_g)\) give, whenever \(0<\theta<(Cb_T)^{-1}\),
\[
\mathbb E e^{\theta V_g}
\le\exp\left\{
\frac{\theta^2\operatorname{Var}(W_g)}{2(1-C\theta b_T)}
\right\}.
\tag{19}
\]
Multiplying (19), applying Chernoff's inequality, and optimizing \(\theta\) for a deviation of order \(Th^d\) gives
\[
P\left\{
\left|\sum_g(W_g-\mathbb EW_g)\right|>cTh^d
\right\}
\le C\exp\left(-c\frac{Th^d}{b_T}\right).
\tag{20}
\]
Apply (20) to both parity families and add the coupling error (17).

For the Gram matrix, apply the resulting scalar bound to \(v^\top\Phi_{z,h}v\) over a fixed \(1/4\)-net \(\mathcal V\) of the unit sphere.  Its cardinality is fixed because \(q_r\) is fixed.  For every symmetric matrix \(A\), approximation of a maximizing eigenvector by \(v\in\mathcal V\) gives
\[
\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2\max_{v\in\mathcal V}|v^\top Av|.
\tag{21}
\]
Equations (14)--(21) show that, outside an event of probability at most
\[
C\exp\left(-c\frac{Th^d}{b_T}\right)+CT^{-A_0},
\tag{22}
\]
the calendar-level mass is at most \(2C_0Th^d\), while the calendar-level Gram matrix is at least \((c_0/2)Th^dI_{q_r}\).  Replication multiplies both quantities by \(n_s\):
\[
L_s(h)=n_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell_{z,h}(X_{st}),
\qquad
G_s(h)=n_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}\Phi_{z,h}(X_{st}).
\tag{23}
\]
Thus the candidate passes the normalized-shape test outside (22), and
\[
P\left\{L_s(h)=0\ \text{or}\
\lambda_{\min}\left(\frac{G_s(h)}{L_s(h)}\right)<c_G
\,\middle|\,E_0,\widetilde z_s\right\}
\le C\exp\left(-c\frac{Th^d}{b_T}\right)+CT^{-A_0}.
\tag{24}
\]
Notice that no response variable and no upper local-mass event occurs in (24).

Write \(h_0=h_{s,\beta}\).  If \(h_0<1\), its definition and a sufficiently large fixed \(C_h\) give
\[
\frac{T(2^vh_0)^d}{b_T}\ge c2^{vd}
\tag{25}
\]
for every dyadic candidate \(2^vh_0\le1\).  If selection has not stopped by that candidate, the candidate fails.  Substituting (25) in (24) proves
\[
P\{h_s>2^vh_{s,\beta}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s\}
\le C\exp(-c2^{vd})+CT^{-A_0}.
\tag{26}
\]
When \(h_0=1\), the assertion is immediate.  At the terminal candidate \(h=1\), (24) gives
\[
P\{\text{terminal-grid failure}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s\}
\le C\exp\{-cT/\log(T\vee2)\}+CT^{-A_0}.
\tag{27}
\]

Fix \(a>0\).  In (16) choose the auxiliary blocking constant large enough to replace \(A_0\) by any \(A_a>a/d+2\); this affects the proof blocks, not the estimator.  The dyadic tail sum and (26) yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P[h_s^a\mathbf1_{\mathrm{good}}\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s]
&\le h_0^a+
\sum_{v:\,2^vh_0<1}(2^{v+1}h_0)^a
P\{h_s>2^vh_0\mid E_0,\widetilde z_s\}\\
&\le Ch_0^a+CT^{-A_a}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{28}
\]
Here \(\sum_{v\ge0}2^{av}e^{-c2^{vd}}<\infty\), and the dyadic values are capped at one.  Expanding the definition of \(h_0\) proves the displayed moment bound.

There is only one selected fit per cohort.  A union bound over fixed \(S\) in (27) controls all selector failures.  Finite fourth donor moment makes \(\bar Z\) and its projection finite almost surely; a successful normalized Gram matrix is invertible; and \(M_4(N)\), \(q_N\), and \(\delta_N\) are finite for every positive \(N\).  Since fixed \(D\) and \(\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}>0\) imply \(q_N\le C\), one has \(\delta_N\le CN^{-1/2}\), so \(\delta_N\le\delta_0\) eventually.  For the finitely many smaller values, the deterministic bad-event indicator is at most \(CR_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Also, because \(A_0>2\lambda/d+2\),
\[
e^{-cT/\log(T\vee2)}+T^{-A_0}
\le C\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{2\lambda/d}
=CR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\tag{29}
\]
Consequently \(P(\mathrm{bad}\mid E_0)\le CR_{\star,\beta}\) along every stated array.  Finally,
\[
T\{(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\}^d
\quad\text{may be }O(1),
\qquad
Th_{s,\beta}^d\ge c\log(T\vee2).
\tag{30}
\]
The second relation, rather than a dense-site hypothesis, supplies (25).  This proves every assertion using geometric mixing of the design alone.

Fix an interior query and one cohort of fixed positive weight.  Hold the remaining cohorts fixed across the two laws.  For sufficiently small fixed \(c_p,c_L>0\), let
\[
L_T=\lfloor c_L\log(T\vee2)\rfloor\vee1,
\qquad
p_T=c_p\frac{L_T}{T},
\]
where \(c_L|\log\rho_0|<1\).  After reducing \(c_p\) if necessary,
\[
2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}
\tag{31}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Let \(A_T\) be a Euclidean ball centered at the chosen cohort block of \(z_0\), contained in \([0,1]^d\), and having Lebesgue measure \(p_T\).  Its radius \(h_T\) obeys
\[
h_T\asymp p_T^{1/d}
\asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{1/d}.
\tag{32}
\]

Partition the calendar into deterministic consecutive blocks of length \(L_T\), apart from a final shorter block.  Independently across blocks draw \(G_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).  Conditional on \(G_b=1\), draw the block's cohort design points independently and uniformly on \(A_T\); conditional on \(G_b=0\), draw them independently and uniformly on \([0,1]^d\setminus A_T\).  Every one-time marginal density is
\[
p_T\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
+(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf1_{A_T^c}(x)}{1-p_T}=1,
\tag{33}
\]
so the stated density bounds hold after the fixed envelope is chosen to contain one.  At lags at least \(L_T\), the relevant design sigma-fields depend on disjoint independent block variables.  At a smaller lag, only a shared block can induce dependence.  Conditional on its Bernoulli state the separated parts are independent, and expansion of the two-component mixture bounds their absolute-regularity distance from the product law by \(2p_T(1-p_T)\le2p_T\).  Thus (31) yields
\[
\beta_P(\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}\mid E_0)
\le
\begin{cases}
2p_T,&1\le\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}<L_T,\\
0,&\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}\ge L_T,
\end{cases}
\le\beta_0\rho_0^{\ell_{\mathrm{mix}}}.
\tag{34}
\]
This verifies the revised, design-only \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}.

Choose a bounded Holder carrier \(g\) lying in the interior of the response range.  When \(\lambda>1\), give \(g\) a nonzero affine component at \(z_0\); when \(0<\lambda\le1\), give it an asymmetric \(\lambda\)-cusp there.  Scale the carrier so its covariance-standardized modulus lies strictly within the declared two-sided envelope.  For a smooth bump \(\psi\) supported on the unit ball with \(\psi(0)=1\), put
\[
m_0(x)=g(x),
\qquad
m_1(x)=g(x)+c_bh_T^\lambda
\psi\left(\frac{x-z_0}{h_T}\right).
\tag{35}
\]
For sufficiently small fixed \(c_b>0\), both surfaces are in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) and stay in the response interior.  If \(\lambda>1\), the bump's increment over a displacement of length \(\delta\) is at most \(Cc_bh_T^{\lambda-1}\delta\) for \(\delta\le h_T\), and at most \(Cc_bh_T^\lambda\le Cc_bh_T^{\lambda-1}\delta\) for \(\delta>h_T\); it therefore cannot cancel the carrier's affine lower modulus.  If \(0<\lambda\le1\), the increment is at most \(Cc_b\delta^\lambda\), so a sufficiently small \(c_b\) cannot cancel the cusp lower modulus.  The Holder upper bound supplies the upper modulus.  Hence both laws satisfy \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus}, with \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).

Conditional on the complete design, draw bounded historical responses independently across units from kernels having mean \(m_\ell(X_{st})\); the kernels may be chosen heterogeneous across units while retaining that common mean.  Their regression errors are centered conditional on the complete design.  Draw bounded event outcomes independently of the design with a common mean under both laws.  Complete untreated event potential outcomes so their cohort-average means are \(m_\ell(z_0)\).  Then
\[
\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]
=\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0],
\qquad
\mathbb E[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid\mathscr X,E_0]=0.
\tag{36}
\]
Take the donor sample iid, independent of the panel, with its covariance and fourth moment strictly inside the fixed envelopes, and take exact historical coordinates.  Define observed and historical potential outcomes by consistency, make historical potential outcomes invariant to the event treatment, and make every potential outcome invariant to other units' assignments.  These choices verify consistency, historical consistency, limited anticipation, no spillovers, event transport, both wealth bounds, cross-unit independence, and all donor and support conditions.  Equations (33)--(36) verify the remaining design, regression, modulus, and full-design-centering properties.  No within-site identical-law property and no response-variance lower bound is required.  Both laws therefore belong to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\).

Let \(\mathcal A_T\) be the event that no calendar block is active.  Since the number of blocks is \(T/L_T+O(1)\),
\[
P(\mathcal A_T\mid E_0)
=(1-p_T)^{T/L_T+O(1)}\longrightarrow e^{-c_p}>0.
\tag{37}
\]
On \(\mathcal A_T\), every design point lies outside \(A_T\), where the two surfaces in (35) agree.  The complete observed-data laws consequently coincide on this event, so
\[
\int\min\{dP_{0,T},dP_{1,T}\}
\ge P(\mathcal A_T\mid E_0)\ge c>0.
\tag{38}
\]
The observed event mean is common, whereas event transport changes the untreated event mean of the selected positive-weight cohort by \(c_bh_T^\lambda\).  The identification formula therefore gives
\[
|\tau_{n,P_{1,T}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{0,T}}(z_0)|
\ge ch_T^\lambda
\asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{\lambda/d}.
\tag{39}
\]
For the finitely many values of \(T\) preceding (31), use a fixed interior ball and two sufficiently close bounded response kernels with a fixed nonzero target separation.  Their testing affinity is positive; since \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\) is bounded on this finite set, decreasing the common constant \(c\) makes (38)--(39) valid for every positive \(T\).
For any estimator, the two error events at half the separation cover the sample space; integrating them against the overlap measure in (38) gives squared risk at least a constant times the square of (39), namely \(cR_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\).  Reducing \(c_p\) makes the affinity in (38) exceed \(2\alpha+a_0\) for some fixed \(a_0>0\).  Any conditionally honest interval covers both target values on a set of overlap measure at least \(a_0\), and hence has expected length at least a constant times (39).  This is \(c_\alpha R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}\), and completes the proof without an anti-clustering premise.

prose_updates.tldr: The target is the cohort-weighted finite-cohort causal buy-and-hold level-wealth effect at a realized event path. Consistency and cohort-average event transport identify it through historical conditional-mean surfaces, and the raw local-polynomial estimator is exactly a cohort-weighted event coefficient. Over the enlarged full-design-centered class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\), bounded unit response laws may be heterogeneous subject only to a common conditional mean, while geometric beta mixing is imposed on the historical design process alone. Matching bounds give conditional mean-squared-error rate \(R_{\star,\beta}\) and expected-length rate \(R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\); the proposed interval is conditionally honest in every finite sample. The feasible construction projects the full independent donor mean once, uses one normalized-shape local-polynomial fit per cohort, and combines bounded unit-cluster Hoeffding radii with exact Holder--Taylor and donor-modulus allowances. The log-adjusted spacing term is unavoidable uniformly, and the donor channel saturates at \(N^{-1}\) in mean squared error when \(\lambda>1\), conditional on the two-sided local modulus.

project_justification.fill: The project proves finite-cohort causal identification under explicit event transport, an exact cohortwise weighted-panel coefficient representation, matching risk and honest-length frontiers over the transparent full-design-centered subclass, and exact finite-sample conditional coverage. A normalized Gram-shape selector under design-only geometric beta mixing, full-data bounded unit-cluster Hoeffding calibration, an exact Taylor allowance, full-sample covariance-standardized donor control, and four channelwise causal-panel witnesses establish the result without donor splitting, sequential overlap, a dense-site condition, an upper local-mass condition, or identical unit response laws.

sampling_model.design: Conditional on \(E_0\), each cohort contributes \(T\) exactly observed pre-event proxy paths with one-time densities bounded above and away from zero. Only the stacked historical design process is geometrically beta mixing. This allows logarithmic blocks of repeated local states and entails the uniform spacing scale \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{1/d}\).
sampling_model.units: At each pre-event path, cohort \(s\) supplies \(n_s\) conditionally independent bounded untreated wealth blocks, and the event date supplies \(n_s\) conditionally independent bounded treated wealth levels. Unit response laws may be heterogeneous across and within cohorts, provided their historical conditional mean is the common \(m_s\); each unit's entire calendar response path is otherwise an unrestricted cluster.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: An independent conditional donor sample of size \(N\) estimates only the event query under a full uniformly elliptic covariance and a fourth-moment envelope; historical training coordinates are exact. The full donor mean is projected once onto the proxy cube and feeds one log-adjusted local-polynomial fit per cohort, selected by normalized Gram shape. The finite-sample conditionally honest interval uses the resulting full-data smoothing weights, separate historical and event bounded-cluster Hoeffding radii, an exact Holder--Taylor allowance, and one full-sample donor-modulus allowance, with \([-B,B]\) fallback on the declared observable bad sample.

prose_updates.related_work: Goldsmith-Pinkham and Lyu (2025) motivate the causal financial-panel setup and the distinction between compounded wealth and linear return effects; their work informs the event-transport layer rather than supplying this frontier. Yan, Yao, and Zhou (2023, revised 2025) provide repeated-measurement Holder rates, while Gaiffas (2007) provides the pointwise random-design local-mass template. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) study generated coordinates attached to training observations, and Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) study replicated classical coordinate error requiring deconvolution; neither observation experiment matches an exact historical design with only a generated query. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) provide the closest conditional synthetic-control uncertainty decomposition and weak-dependence tools, here applied only to the historical design. Armstrong and Kolesar (2018) motivate modulus-based honest length. The present proof instead uses full-sample donor calibration, arbitrary bounded within-unit response histories, and an explicit rare-block design witness.
prose_updates.interpretation: For every integer \(T\ge3\), the replicated-smoothing term obeys \(R_{\mathrm{sm}}\le aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\le R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\), where \(a=2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)\). Hence the active risk is exactly \(R_{\star,\beta}=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\): smoothing remains useful bookkeeping but is never uniquely active. The oracle region has \(N^{-\kappa}=o(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta})\), the generated-proxy region reverses that relation, and the boundary equates the two. The sole donor elbow is \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\). The iid spacing expression \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\) applies only under independent design, or a separately imposed fixed-query local-small-ball or anti-clustering condition that delivers it.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Causal identification remains conditional on the maintained event-transport equality. The risk and honest-length results additionally use the two explicit full-design mean-stability and historical-centering restrictions defining \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\); neither follows from contemporaneous regression centering or conditional cross-unit independence. Geometric beta mixing is required only for the historical design, and bounded unit response paths may otherwise be arbitrarily dependent over time and heterogeneous across units subject to their common conditional mean. The two-sided local modulus is assumed rather than derived over the whole Holder ball, so flat surfaces are outside the donor lower-bound subclass. The results keep \(S\) and \(p(H+1)\) fixed and do not provide smoothness adaptation or sharp minimax constants.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved contribution consists of event-transport identification, the exact full-donor FWL identity, normalized-shape local-polynomial control, a log-adjusted selector bound under design-only geometric beta mixing, a positive-affinity rare-block spacing obstruction, four causal-panel lower-bound embeddings, a matching conditional-risk frontier, and an exact finite-sample conditionally honest interval with asymptotically optimal expected length over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)\). Historical and event unit response laws may be heterogeneous and each unit's calendar history is treated as one bounded cluster. No donor splitting, covariance estimation, response-variance lower bound, sequential overlap, dense-local-site, upper-local-mass, studentization, or temporal-outcome mixing condition is used. The donor converse remains conditional on the two-sided local modulus, and causal interpretation remains conditional on event transport.

Write \(a=a_{\mathrm w}\).  We give a common measurable scaffolding, conditional on \(E_0\), on which only the sign-pair kernels vary with \(\rho\in\mathcal R\).  Fix the displayed
\[
z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\cap[\delta_0,1-\delta_0]^d.
\]
Let \(X_{1t}\), \(t=1,\ldots,T\), be independent uniform random vectors on \([0,1]^d\), conditional on \(E_0\).  Conditional on the complete design and \(E_0\), draw the historical sign pairs independently over \((t,i)\) according to
\[
P_\rho(U_{1ti}=u,V_{1ti}=v\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
=\frac{1+\rho(x)uv}{4},
\qquad (u,v)\in\{-1,1\}^2.
\]
The defining bound \(\sup_x|\rho(x)|\le 1-2\delta_0\) for \(\mathcal R\) implies
\[
\frac{1+\rho(x)uv}{4}\ge \frac{1-\lvert\rho(x)\rvert}{4}
\ge\frac{\delta_0}{2}>0,
\]
and summing the four displayed masses gives one.  Thus this is a well-defined, everywhere-positive conditional kernel.  Independently over \(i\), and independently of all historical variables given \(E_0\), draw \((U_{1i},V_{1i})\) from the same kernel evaluated at \(x=z_0\); use that kernel for every \(x\in[0,1]^d\) to specify the regular conditional event-sign law away from the realized point as well.  Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
B_{1i}(0)&=(1+aU_{1i})(1+aV_{1i}),
&B_{1i}(1)&=B_{1i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=1,\\
Q_{1ti}(0)&=Q_{1ti}(1)=Q_{1ti},
&Q_{1ti}&=(1+aU_{1ti})(1+aV_{1ti}).
\end{aligned}
\]
Set \(W_{1i,-1}=1\), \(R_{1i0}(0)=aU_{1i}\), \(R_{1i1}(0)=aV_{1i}\), and \(R_{1ih}(1)=0\) for \(h=0,1\).  By \texttt{def:buyhold-level}, these choices give the displayed values of \(B_{1i}(0)\) and \(B_{1i}(1)\).  Since \(0<a<1\), every return is strictly larger than \(-1\).  For every other-unit assignment vector, set
\[
B_{1i}(b,\mathbf a_{-1i})=B_{1i}(b),\qquad b\in\{0,1\}.
\]
The preceding equations verify \texttt{ass:consistency}, \texttt{ass:historical-consistency}, \texttt{ass:no-spillovers}, and \texttt{ass:limited-anticipation}.

We next complete the donor law without replacing the full covariance by coordinatewise variances.  Because \(S=1\), the stacked donor dimension is \(Sd=d\).  Conditional on \(E_0\), let \(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_N\) be independent and uniform on the Euclidean sphere of radius \(\sqrt d\) in \(\mathbb R^d\), independent of the complete historical and event panels, and put
\[
Z_j=z_0+\xi_j.
\]
For any orthogonal matrix \(O\), rotational invariance gives \(O\xi_j\overset d=\xi_j\).  Hence \(\mathbb E(\xi_j\mid E_0)=0\), and \(A:=\mathbb E(\xi_j\xi_j^\top\mid E_0)\) commutes with every orthogonal matrix, so \(A=cI_d\) for some \(c\).  Taking traces yields
\[
dc=\operatorname{tr}(A)
=\mathbb E(\lVert\xi_j\rVert_2^2\mid E_0)=d,
\]
and therefore
\[
\mathbb E(Z_j\mid E_0)=z_0,
\qquad
\Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid E_0)=I_d.
\]
In particular \(\Sigma\) has rank \(d\), and the declared ranges \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\) imply
\[
c_\Sigma I_d\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_d.
\]
Moreover, the hypothesis \(B\ge d^2\) gives
\[
\mathbb E_{P_\rho}\!\left[
 \left\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\right\|_2^4
 \mathrel{\big|}E_0\right]
=\mathbb E(\lVert\xi_j\rVert_2^4\mid E_0)
=d^2\le B.
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:donor-replication}, \texttt{ass:donor-independence}, \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}, and \texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment} all hold for the full stacked donor path.

We now compute the historical response surface rather than identifying it by definition.  Summing the four-point kernel gives, for every \(x\in[0,1]^d\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{P_\rho}(U_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)&=0,\\
\mathbb E_{P_\rho}(V_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)&=0,\\
\mathbb E_{P_\rho}(U_{1ti}V_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)&=\rho(x).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{P_\rho}(Q_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
&=\mathbb E_{P_\rho}\!\left[
1+a(U_{1ti}+V_{1ti})+a^2U_{1ti}V_{1ti}
\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0\right]\\
&=1+a^2\rho(x).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus, by \texttt{ass:historical-regression}, the regression surface is
\[
m_1^{P_\rho}(x)=1+a^2\rho(x).
\]
The compatibility hypothesis \(\{1+a^2\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}\subset\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) verifies \texttt{ass:holder-smoothness}.  Since \(H=1\) and \(p\ge1\), the identity \(d=p(H+1)\) gives \(d=2p\ge2\).  Hence
\[
0<(1-a)^2\le Q_{1ti}\le(1+a)^2<4\le d^2\le B.
\]
The same inequalities hold for \(B_{1i}(0)\), while \(B_{1i}(1)=1\le B\).  This proves \texttt{ass:bounded-historical-wealth} and \texttt{ass:bounded-event-wealth}.

The maintained class does not require a common within-site response law or a response-variance lower bound, but this particular witness has both properties.  Indeed, its conditional kernel is the same for every \(i\).  Also, for \(r=\rho(x)\), write \(U=U_{1ti}\) and \(V=V_{1ti}\).  The identities
\[
\mathbb E(U+V)=0,
\quad \mathbb E(UV)=r,
\quad (U+V)^2=2+2UV,
\quad (U+V)UV=U+V
\]
hold under the conditional kernel at \(x\).  Since subtracting the conditional mean does not change variance,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}_{P_\rho}(Q_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)
&=\operatorname{Var}\{a(U+V)+a^2UV\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0\}\\
&=a^2\mathbb E\{(U+V)^2\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0\}
  +a^4\operatorname{Var}(UV\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0)\\
&\quad+2a^3\mathbb E\{(U+V)(UV-r)\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0\}\\
&=2a^2(1+r)+a^4(1-r^2).
\end{aligned}
\]
The cross term is zero because \(\mathbb E\{(U+V)UV\}=\mathbb E(U+V)=0\).  The displayed hypothesis in the proposition therefore implies that this variance is at least \(B^{-1}\), uniformly in \(\rho\) and \(x\).  This calculation merely certifies nondegeneracy of the selected lower-bound witness; it is not invoked as a restriction on the enlarged panel-law class.

It remains to verify the other class conditions.  The uniform design has density one, so the declared inequalities \(c_X\le1\le C_X\) imply \texttt{ass:design-density}.  Conditional independence of the complete unit-level sign collections over \(i\), together with the independent event collections, gives \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} after conditioning on the complete design and \(E_0\).  The design and historical sign pairs were drawn independently across \(t\), so the complete calendar vectors are conditionally independent across time; in particular, the historical design sequence \((X_{1t})_{t=1}^T\) is conditionally independent.  Therefore its absolute-regularity coefficients satisfy
\[
\beta_{P_\rho}(k\mid E_0)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k,
\qquad k\ge1,
\]
which is the design-only form of \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}; no restriction on within-unit temporal outcome dependence is used.  Set \(X_{1t}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{1t}\) to obtain \texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates}.  The stipulated location of \(z_0\) gives
\[
\operatorname{dist}(z_0,\partial[0,1]^d)\ge\delta_0,
\]
and hence \texttt{ass:interior-event-path}.  Choose the conditional event state to be degenerate at this admissible configuration.  Then
\[
P_\rho\{z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\}=1\ge c_X,
\]
so \texttt{ass:positive-query-region} holds.  Finally, the definition of \(\mathcal R\) states that the induced surface \(x\mapsto1+a^2\rho(x)\) satisfies the maintained two-sided covariance-standardized local-modulus inequalities.  Since the full covariance just calculated is \(I_d\), this is exactly \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus}, with \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).

For event transport, the untreated event signs have the historical kernel evaluated at \(z_0\).  Applying the preceding conditional-mean calculation at that point gives, for every \(i\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P_\rho}[B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]
=1+a^2\rho(z_0)
=m_1^{P_\rho}(z_0).
\]
Averaging over \(i=1,\ldots,n_1\) proves \texttt{ass:event-transport}.  We have verified every member property in \texttt{def:panel-law-class}.  The construction additionally has common within-site conditional laws and nondegenerate conditional response variance, although neither property restricts the enlarged class.  Hence
\[
\{P_\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}
\subset\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(\lambda).
\]
The indexing set is nonempty and relatively open by the definition of \(\mathcal R\).

We next derive the causal estimand and keep it distinct from the observed historical regression.  Since \(S=1\) and \(\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s=1\), one has \(\pi_1=1\).  By \texttt{def:target}, the potential-outcome construction, and the event-transport identity just proved,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_{n,P_\rho}(z_0)
&=\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
\mathbb E_{P_\rho}[B_{1i}(1)-B_{1i}(0)\mid z_0,E_0]\\
&=1-\{1+a^2\rho(z_0)\}\\
&=-a^2\rho(z_0).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the causal equality follows from potential outcomes and event transport; it is not introduced as an observed-law definition.

We finally compare the restricted information maps.  Marginalizing the sign-pair kernel yields
\[
P_\rho(U=u\mid x,E_0)
=\sum_{v\in\{-1,1\}}\frac{1+\rho(x)uv}{4}
=\frac12,
\qquad
P_\rho(V=v\mid x,E_0)=\frac12.
\]
Therefore each untreated return coordinate has, conditional on every \(x\), the common symmetric distribution on \(\{-a,a\}\), and in particular conditional mean zero.  Every treated return coordinate is identically zero.  The initial-wealth law is the common point mass at one, and
\[
\mathbb E_{P_\rho}[B_{1i}(1)\mid z_0,E_0]=1
\]
for every \(\rho\).  It follows directly from \texttt{def:mean-only-information} that \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_\rho)\) is constant over \(\rho\in\mathcal R\).

It remains to show that this constant-information family contains a target-separated pair.  Choose \(\rho_*\in\mathcal R\), possible because \(\mathcal R\ne\varnothing\).  Relative openness in the Holder ball supplies \(\epsilon>0\) such that
\[
\left\{g\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L):
\lVert g-\rho_*\rVert_{\mathcal H_d}<\epsilon\right\}
\subset\mathcal R.
\]
There is a constant function \(c\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\) with \(c\ne\rho_*(z_0)\): among two distinct constants of sufficiently small absolute value, at most one equals \(\rho_*(z_0)\).  For \(0<\eta<1\), define
\[
\rho_\eta=(1-\eta)\rho_*+\eta c.
\]
The Holder ball is convex, so \(\rho_\eta\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\), and
\[
\lVert\rho_\eta-\rho_*\rVert_{\mathcal H_d}
=\eta\lVert c-\rho_*\rVert_{\mathcal H_d}<\epsilon
\]
for every sufficiently small \(\eta>0\).  Hence \(\rho_\eta\in\mathcal R\), while
\[
\rho_\eta(z_0)-\rho_*(z_0)
=\eta\{c-\rho_*(z_0)\}\ne0.
\]
Set \(\rho^{(0)}=\rho_*\) and \(\rho^{(1)}=\rho_\eta\).  Constancy of the restricted information map gives
\[
\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho^{(0)}})
=\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho^{(1)}}),
\]
whereas the causal-target formula gives
\[
\left|\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(1)}}}(z_0)
-\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(0)}}}(z_0)\right|
=a^2\left|\rho^{(1)}(z_0)-\rho^{(0)}(z_0)\right|>0.
\]
No functional of \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}\) can therefore equal \(\tau_n\) throughout this submodel.  The full historical wealth laws need not be equal: the joint sign kernel, and generally the conditional law of \(Q_{1ti}\), varies with \(\rho\).  The obstruction is exactly loss of within-path dependence information under the restricted mean-only map, as claimed.

proposed.statement:
Consider the one-cohort, two-return specialization \(S=1\) and \(H=1\), so that \(d=2p\), and fix
\[
 z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\cap[\delta_0,1-\delta_0]^d.
\]
Suppose, in addition to \(0<a_{\mathrm w}<1\), that
\[
 B\ge d^2,\qquad
 \inf_{\rho\in\mathcal R}\inf_{x\in[0,1]^d}
 \left[2a_{\mathrm w}^2\{1+\rho(x)\}
       +a_{\mathrm w}^4\{1-\rho(x)^2\}\right]\ge B^{-1},
 \qquad
 \{1+a_{\mathrm w}^2\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}
 \subset\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L).
\]
Then the construction in \texttt{def:mean-only-witness} has a common completion for which the \(\rho\)-indexed, relatively open family
\[
 \{P_\rho:\rho\in\mathcal R\}
 \subset\mathcal M_{N,T,(n_1)}(\lambda).
\]
For every \(\rho\in\mathcal R\) and \(x\in[0,1]^d\), the untreated return-coordinate means are zero and their conditional coordinate marginals do not depend on \(\rho\), whereas
\[
 m_1^{P_\rho}(x)
 =\mathbb E_{P_\rho}[Q_{1ti}\mid X_{1t}=x,E_0]
 =1+a_{\mathrm w}^2\rho(x),
 \qquad
 \tau_{n,P_\rho}(z_0)=-a_{\mathrm w}^2\rho(z_0).
\]
There consequently exist \(\rho^{(0)},\rho^{(1)}\in\mathcal R\) such that \(\rho^{(0)}(z_0)\ne\rho^{(1)}(z_0)\),
\[
 \mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho^{(0)}})
 =\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}(P_{\rho^{(1)}}),
 \qquad
 \left|\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(1)}}}(z_0)-\tau_{n,P_{\rho^{(0)}}}(z_0)\right|
 =a_{\mathrm w}^2\left|\rho^{(1)}(z_0)-\rho^{(0)}(z_0)\right|>0.
\]
Thus \(\tau_n\) is not a functional of \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{mean}}\) on this submodel. This conclusion concerns only mean-only return-path matching; it does not assert observational equivalence under the full historical wealth panel.
proposed.justification: The result isolates the information loss from discarding within-path dependence without denying identification from the maintained full wealth panel.
proposed.gap: Barber--Lyon and Goldsmith-Pinkham--Lyu diagnose volatility drag; this proposition gives an explicit two-law, relatively open nonidentification result for the restricted mean-only map while preserving full-panel identification under event transport.
proposed.consumer: Analysts can determine whether a return-matching procedure discards dependence information needed for a finite-cohort compounded-wealth effect.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The enlarged class deletes within-site replication and a response-variance lower bound. This replacement removes only those obsolete dependency edges and leaves the formal claim unchanged.

Put
\[
a:=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}\in(0,1),
\qquad
q:=\frac{2\lambda}{d}>0.
\]
These ranges follow from \(\lambda>0\) and \(d>0\).  We first establish the weighted arithmetic--geometric mean inequality used below.  For \(u>0\), define
\[
\phi(u):=au+(1-a)-u^a.
\]
Then \(\phi(1)=0\) and
\[
\phi'(u)=a\bigl(1-u^{a-1}\bigr).
\]
Because \(a-1<0\), the derivative is negative on \((0,1)\) and positive on \((1,\infty)\).  Hence \(u=1\) is a global minimizer, so \(\phi(u)\geq0\).  Taking \(u=x/y\) and multiplying by \(y>0\) proves
\[
x^a y^{1-a}\leq ax+(1-a)y,
\qquad x,y>0.
\]

The definitions of \(a\) and \(q\) give
\[
q(1-a)
=\frac{2\lambda}{d}\frac{d}{2\lambda+d}
=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}
=a.
\]
For every cohort \(s\), positivity of the integers \(T\) and \(n_s\) permits the preceding inequality with \(x=n_s^{-1}\) and \(y=T^{-q}\).  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
&=n_s^{-a}T^{-a}\\
&=(n_s^{-1})^a(T^{-q})^{1-a}\\
&\leq a n_s^{-1}+(1-a)T^{-q}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Multiplication by \(\pi_s^2\), summation over \(s\), and the definitions in \texttt{def:rate-frontier} yield
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)T^{-q}\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s^2.
\]
The cohort weights are positive and satisfy \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\), whence
\[
\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s^2
\leq \left(\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s\right)^2
=1.
\]
Since \(T\geq1\), one has \(\log(T\vee2)\geq\log2>0\).  Thus, by the definition of \(R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\),
\[
T^{-q}
\leq(\log2)^{-q}
\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{q}
=(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\]
It follows that
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
&\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}
+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\\
&\leq
\bigl\{a+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}\bigr\}
\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr)\\
&=C_{\lambda,d}
\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(0<\log2<1\) and \(q>0\), one also has
\[
C_{\lambda,d}=a+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}\geq a+(1-a)=1.
\]

Let
\[
A:=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta},
\qquad
D_0:=A\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
All rate components are positive.  The definition of \(R_{\star,\beta}\) and the bound just proved imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_0
&\leq R_{\star,\beta}\\
&=A\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\\
&\leq D_0\vee(C_{\lambda,d}A)\\
&\leq C_{\lambda,d}D_0.
\end{aligned}
\]
The last inequality uses \(C_{\lambda,d}\geq1\) and \(A\leq D_0\).  Hence
\[
R_{\star,\beta}
\asymp_{\lambda,d}
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}},
\]
with comparison constants \(1\) and \(C_{\lambda,d}\), independent of \(N\), \(T\), \(S\), and the positive replication counts.

The stronger eventual identity follows from the same calculation.  If \(T\geq3\), then \(T\vee2=T\) and \(\log T\geq1\); consequently
\[
T^{-q}\leq\left(\frac{\log T}{T}\right)^q
=R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\]
Therefore
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}
\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta},
\]
where the final inequality holds because \(a\in(0,1)\).  Substitution into the defining maximum gives, exactly for every integer \(T\geq3\),
\[
R_{\star,\beta}
=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]

By \texttt{def:rate-frontier}, \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa}\).  Along any joint growth array, this channel is negligible relative to \(A\) precisely when
\[
N^{-\kappa}=o(A),
\]
and it dominates \(A\) precisely when
\[
A=o(N^{-\kappa}).
\]
Because \(\kappa>0\), the boundary relation \(N^{-\kappa}\asymp A\) is equivalent to
\[
N\asymp A^{-1/\kappa}.
\]
Indeed, applying the strictly decreasing map \(x\mapsto x^{-1/\kappa}\) to a positive two-sided constant comparison reverses both inequalities and preserves a two-sided constant comparison.  These are minimax phases only when a separate statistical result establishes \(R_{\star,\beta}\) as the sharp risk; the present deductions are algebraic.

Under independent design, or under a separately imposed fixed-query local-small-ball/anti-clustering condition that delivers \(R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-q}\), the cohortwise inequality instead gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_{\mathrm{sm}}
&\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp}}\sum_{s=1}^S\pi_s^2\\
&\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp}}\\
&\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Using this inequality in the comparator definition of \(R_\star\) yields both
\[
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}
\leq R_\star
\]
and
\[
R_\star
=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}
\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Thus
\[
R_\star=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]

Assumption \texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates} states
\[
X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}.
\]
Thus the historical design is observed without classical covariate measurement error, so evaluation of the historical-design procedure does not require inversion of a measurement-error convolution.  Direct inspection of the exhaustive rate-component list in \texttt{def:rate-frontier} shows that the stated bookkeeping contains neither a deconvolution term nor a separate moving-Gram term.  This is a consequence only about the observation structure and the defined bookkeeping, not a statistical sharpness assertion.

Finally, \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\).  If \(\lambda>1\), then \(\kappa=1\), and hence
\[
R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa}=N^{-1}.
\]
This establishes all asserted relations, including the exact identity for \(T\geq3\), the oracle/generated-center boundary, and the sole donor elbow at \(\lambda=1\).

It is enough to exhibit one admissible triangular array.  Throughout the proof, suppress the unique cohort index.  Fix
\[
H=0,\qquad p=S=d=1,\qquad \lambda=\kappa=1,
\qquad \pi_1=1,
\]
and choose
\[
B=16,\qquad c_X=C_X=c_\Sigma=C_\Sigma=1,
\qquad \delta_0=\frac14,
\qquad c_{\mathrm{mod}}=C_{\mathrm{mod}}=1.
\]
Take the H\"older radius \(L\) large enough to contain the affine regression defined below.  Let
\[
K(u)={\bf 1}\{|u|\leq1\}.
\]
Then \(r=\lceil\lambda\rceil-1=0\), \(b_0(u)=1\), and the normalized local-design threshold may be chosen with \(0<c_G\leq1\).  Let \(E_0\) be constant, set \(z_0=1/2\), and put \(\mathcal Z_+=\{1/2\}\).  For each integer \(T\geq1\), set
\[
n_1=N=T^2.
\]

We first construct the historical panel.  Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_T\) be independent uniform random variables on \([0,1]\), define
\[
m(x)=8+x-\frac12,
\qquad
Q_{ti}=m(X_t)+\frac12U_{ti},
\]
and take the variables \((U_{ti})_{t,i}\) to be independent Rademacher variables independent of the complete design.  Thus
\[
7\leq Q_{ti}\leq9\leq B,
\qquad
\mathbb E[Q_{ti}\mid X_t,E_0]=m(X_t).
\]
The first display verifies \(\texttt{ass:bounded-historical-wealth}\), and the second verifies \(\texttt{ass:historical-regression}\).  The affine map \(m\) is in \(\mathcal H_1(1,L)\), as required by \(\texttt{ass:holder-smoothness}\).  The conditional density is identically one, so \(\texttt{ass:design-density}\) holds.  Moreover, the design process \((X_t)_{t=1}^T\) is independent over calendar time.  Its conditional absolute-regularity coefficients therefore satisfy
\[
\beta_P(k\mid E_0)=0\leq\beta_0\rho_0^k,
\qquad k\geq1,
\]
which verifies the design-only version of \(\texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}\).  No condition on temporal dependence of the outcome path is needed for the proposition.

Independently of the entire panel, let
\[
Z_j=\frac12+V_j,
\]
where \(V_1,\ldots,V_N\) are independent Rademacher variables.  It follows that
\[
\mathbb E[Z_j\mid E_0]=z_0,
\qquad
\Sigma=\operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid E_0)=1,
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E\!left[|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)|^4\mid E_0\right]=1\leq B.
\]
Thus \(\texttt{ass:donor-independence}\), \(\texttt{ass:donor-replication}\), \(\texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity}\), and \(\texttt{ass:donor-fourth-moment}\) hold.  Define \(X_t^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_t\), which verifies \(\texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates}\).

The local modulus can be evaluated exactly.  For \(0<\delta\leq\delta_0\), the perturbations \(z_0+u\) with \(|u|\leq\delta\) remain in \([0,1]\), and the definition of the full-covariance modulus gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\omega_P(\delta;z_0)
&=\sup_{|u|\leq\delta}|m(z_0+u)-m(z_0)|\\
&=\sup_{|u|\leq\delta}|u|=\delta.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves \(\texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus}\) with the displayed constants.  Also,
\[
\operatorname{dist}(z_0,\partial[0,1])=\frac12\geq\delta_0,
\qquad
P\{z_0\in\mathcal Z_+\}=1\geq c_X,
\]
so \(\texttt{ass:interior-event-path}\) and \(\texttt{ass:positive-query-region}\) hold.

We next construct the event outcomes.  Put
\[
G={\bf 1}\{X_1\leq1/4\},
\qquad
B_i(0)=8,
\qquad
B_i(1)=8+G,
\qquad
B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_i(1).
\]
Define \(B_i(a,\mathbf a_{-i})=B_i(a)\), and define every historical potential outcome \(Q_{ti}(a)\) to equal \(Q_{ti}\).  These definitions verify, respectively, \(\texttt{ass:consistency}\), \(\texttt{ass:historical-consistency}\), \(\texttt{ass:no-spillovers}\), and \(\texttt{ass:limited-anticipation}\).  They also imply
\[
0\leq B_i(a)\leq9\leq B,
\]
as required by \(\texttt{ass:bounded-event-wealth}\).  The construction is compatible with \(\texttt{def:buyhold-level}\): take \(W_{i,-1}=1\) and \(R_{i0}(a)=B_i(a)-1>-1\), so that
\[
W_{i,-1}\{1+R_{i0}(a)\}=B_i(a).
\]
Since \(m(z_0)=8\),
\[
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
\mathbb E[B_i(0)\mid z_0,E_0]=8=m(z_0),
\]
which proves \(\texttt{ass:event-transport}\).

Conditional on the complete design and \(E_0\), every \(B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is constant, while the historical path of unit \(i\) depends only on \((U_{ti})_{t=1}^T\).  The latter vectors are independent across \(i\).  Hence
\[
((Q_{ti})_{t=1}^T,B_i^{\mathrm{obs}})
\perp
((Q_{ti'})_{t=1}^T,B_{i'}^{\mathrm{obs}})
\mid (X_t)_{t=1}^T,E_0,
\qquad i\ne i',
\]
which is exactly \(\texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence}\).  We have now checked every member property of the weakened class in \(\texttt{def:panel-law-class}\).  In particular, neither identical conditional response laws across units nor a response-variance lower bound was used.

Because \(z_0\) and \(E_0\) are constant and \(G\) is Bernoulli with success probability \(1/4\), \(\texttt{def:target}\) yields
\[
\tau_n(z_0)
=\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
\mathbb E[B_i(1)-B_i(0)\mid z_0,E_0]
=\mathbb E[G]=\frac14,
\]
whereas
\[
\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}=8+G.
\]

We now analyze the all-donor estimator in \(\texttt{def:feasible-estimator}\).  Let
\[
\bar Z=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^N Z_j,
\qquad
\widetilde z=\Pi_{[0,1]}(\bar Z).
\]
Projection onto \([0,1]\) is nonexpansive and fixes \(z_0\).  Therefore
\[
|\widetilde z-z_0|
\leq|\bar Z-z_0|
=\left|N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NV_j\right|,
\]
and donor independence gives
\[
\mathbb E[(\widetilde z-z_0)^2\mid E_0]
\leq N^{-1}=T^{-2}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\), the initial bandwidth is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\underline h_T=h_{1,\beta}
&=C_h\left[(Tn_1)^{-1/3}
\vee\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}
\vee N^{-1/2}\right]\\
&=C_h\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T<1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Conditional on \(\widetilde z\in[0,1]\), the interval
\([\widetilde z-\underline h_T,\widetilde z+\underline h_T]\cap[0,1]\)
has Lebesgue measure at least \(\underline h_T\).  Define
\[
I_T=\{t:|X_t-\widetilde z|\leq\underline h_T\},
\qquad
\mathcal A_T=\{|I_T|>0\}.
\]
The uniform independent design and donor independence imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0,\widetilde z)
&\leq(1-\underline h_T)^T\\
&\leq\exp(-T\underline h_T),
\end{aligned}
\]
and consequently \(P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)\to0\).  On \(\mathcal A_T\), the degree-zero normalized Gram ratio at the initial bandwidth is
\[
\frac{G_1(\underline h_T)}{L_1(\underline h_T)}=1\geq c_G.
\]
Thus the selector chooses \(h_1=\underline h_T\), and its fitted intercept equals
\[
\widehat m_1
=\frac1{n_1|I_T|}
\sum_{t\in I_T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}Q_{ti}.
\]
The conditional-mean part obeys
\[
\left|
\frac1{|I_T|}\sum_{t\in I_T}m(X_t)-m(z_0)
\right|
\leq \underline h_T+|\widetilde z-z_0|,
\]
because \(|X_t-\widetilde z|\leq\underline h_T\) on \(I_T\) and \(m(x)-m(z_0)=x-z_0\).  Conditional on the design and donors, the regression-error part has mean zero and variance
\[
\operatorname{Var}\!\left(
\frac1{2n_1|I_T|}\sum_{t\in I_T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}U_{ti}
\,\middle|\,(X_t)_{t=1}^T,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^N
\right)
=\frac1{4n_1|I_T|}
\leq\frac1{4n_1}.
\]
Every successful degree-zero intercept lies in \([0,B]\), and the definition assigns zero after selector failure.  The preceding bounds and boundedness on \(\mathcal A_T^c\) therefore give a constant \(C<\infty\), independent of \(T\), such that
\[
\mathbb E[(\widehat m_1-m(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
\leq C\left\{
\underline h_T^2+N^{-1}+n_1^{-1}
+P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)
\right\}\longrightarrow0.
\]

Using \(\widehat\tau=\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat m_1\), we obtain the exact decomposition
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)
=G-\frac14-\{\widehat m_1-m(z_0)\}.
\]
The last brace converges to zero in conditional \(L^2\).  By Cauchy--Schwarz, its cross term with the bounded variable \(G-1/4\) also converges to zero.  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
\lim_{T\to\infty}
\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0]
&=\mathbb E[(G-1/4)^2\mid E_0]\\
&=\frac14\left(1-\frac14\right)=\frac{3}{16}.
\end{aligned}
\]

For this array, every component in the iid-design comparator frontier of \(\texttt{def:rate-frontier}\) is equal to \(T^{-2}\):
\[
R_{\mathrm{tr}}=n_1^{-1}=T^{-2},
\]
\[
R_{\mathrm{sm}}=(Tn_1)^{-2/3}=(T^3)^{-2/3}=T^{-2},
\]
and
\[
R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-1}=T^{-2}.
\]
Therefore \(R_\star=T^{-2}\).

For the event multiplier calculation, all event outcomes have the common realized value \(8+G\).  Consequently
\[
E_{1i}=\frac1{n_1}
\{B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\}=0
\qquad(1\leq i\leq n_1).
\]
It follows from the definitions of \(G_{\mathrm{tr}}^{\#}\) and \(r_{\mathrm{tr}}\) that
\[
G_{\mathrm{tr}}^{\#}=0,
\qquad
r_{\mathrm{tr}}=0
\]
almost surely.  On the other hand, the centered event-average contribution is
\[
\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}
-\mathbb E[\bar B_1^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]
=G-\frac14,
\]
whose conditional variance is \(3/16\).

It remains to analyze \(C_\alpha\) from \(\texttt{def:honest-interval}\).  On \(\mathcal A_T\), the successful degree-zero weights are
\[
a_{ti}=\frac{{\bf 1}\{t\in I_T\}}{n_1|I_T|}.
\]
They are nonnegative and satisfy
\[
\sum_{t=1}^Ta_{ti}=\frac1{n_1},
\qquad
\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}a_{ti}=1.
\]
Thus the historical and event Hoeffding radii obey
\[
\begin{aligned}
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
&=B\left\{
\frac12\log\left(\frac2{\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}}\right)
n_1\left(\frac1{n_1}\right)^2
\right\}^{1/2}
=O(T^{-1}),\\
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
&=B\left\{
\frac12\log\left(\frac2{\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}}\right)
\frac1{n_1}
\right\}^{1/2}
=O(T^{-1}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The exact Taylor allowance satisfies
\[
\begin{aligned}
A_L
&=C_{0,1}L
\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}
a_{ti}|X_t-\widetilde z|\\
&\leq C_{0,1}L\underline h_T
=O\!\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right).
\end{aligned}
\]

For the exact full-sample donor calibration, \(D=1\), and hence
\[
M_4(N)=\frac{16}{N}
+3\left(1-\frac1N\right)
=3+\frac{13}{N}\leq16.
\]
Therefore, for fixed \(\alpha\),
\[
q_N=\{M_4(N)/\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}\}^{1/4}=O(1),
\qquad
\delta_N=\sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,q_NN^{-1/2}=O(T^{-1}),
\]
and the upper local modulus gives
\[
A_{\mathrm{don}}=C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta_N^\kappa=O(T^{-1}).
\]
In particular, \(\delta_N\leq\delta_0\) for every sufficiently large \(T\).  On \(\mathcal A_T\), the selected Gram matrix is positive and all weights and radii are finite.  Thus, under the all-donor construction, none of the declared bad-sample conditions occurs on \(\mathcal A_T\) for all sufficiently large \(T\).  Combining the four radius bounds yields
\[
H_\alpha{\bf 1}_{\mathcal A_T}
=O\!\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right)=o(1),
\qquad
P(\text{bad sample}\mid E_0)
\leq P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)\longrightarrow0.
\]

Finally,
\[
\widehat\tau-G=8-\widehat m_1\longrightarrow0
\]
in conditional probability, while \(|G-1/4|\geq1/4\) almost surely.  On \(\mathcal A_T\), if
\[
|\widehat\tau-G|<\frac1{16}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
H_\alpha<\frac18,
\]
then
\[
|\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0)|
\geq |G-1/4|-|\widehat\tau-G|
\geq\frac3{16}>H_\alpha,
\]
so \(\tau_n(z_0)\notin C_\alpha\).  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}
&\leq P(\mathcal A_T^c\mid E_0)
+P\{|\widehat\tau-G|\geq1/16\mid E_0\}\\
&\quad+P\{H_\alpha\geq1/8,\mathcal A_T\mid E_0\}
\longrightarrow0.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves every assertion of the proposition.

proposed.statement:
For an admissible fixed choice of class constants with \(H=0\), \(p=S=d=1\), \(\lambda=\kappa=1\), and the uniform order-zero kernel \(K\), there is a triangular array of laws in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(\lambda)\), with \(n_1=N=T^2\), for which
\[
R_\star=T^{-2},\qquad
\lim_{T\to\infty}\mathbb E\!\left[(\widehat\tau-\tau_n(z_0))^2\mid E_0\right]=\frac{3}{16}.
\]
In the same array, the event multiplier radius satisfies \(r_{\mathrm{tr}}=0\) almost surely even though the conditional variance of the centered event contribution is \(3/16\).
Moreover, for every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\),
\[
P\{\tau_n(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid E_0\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
